text:
Sarah: quick RFC follow-up: we need a firm default for tenant private connectivity. two clear paths: place a private endpoint resource in the customer VPC (direct) or terminate in our tenant-proxy fleet and backhaul. want to capture tradeoffs + a default.

Matt: TL;DR constraints i care about: predictable latency, customer firewall simplicity, scaling ops, and cert lifecycle.

Oliver: direct = best latency, simpler for customers who want source-IP preservation, but it multiplies cross-account endpoint count and peering complexity.

Devon: proxy = easier to centralize telemetry, do request-level caching, and implement canary rollouts. downside: an extra network hop and more infra to operate.

Priya: from SRE POV proxy gives us a clear failover surface. if a direct endpoint flaps due to a customer route change we have no automatic fallback. with proxy we can circuit-break and route to hosted endpoints.

Matt: cost framing: direct -> per-customer infra footprint (ENIs, route tables), proxy -> shared CPU/GPU and egress costs. ops headcount vs infra bill tradeoff.

Sarah: security/certs: direct typically needs tenant-scoped certs or mTLS to verify client identity. proxy allows us to reuse platform certs but we then need strong attestation between proxy and control plane to prevent impersonation.

Oliver: routing detail: many downstream partners require true source IP on egress. XFF headers won't cut it for their ACLs. those customers must be direct.

Devon: we proposed a hybrid earlier but left thresholds fuzzy. propose we pick numeric thresholds and explicit opt-ins.

Sarah: candidate policy options:
- Policy 1 (direct-first): create direct endpoints by default; enable proxy in cases of high throughput, onboarding issues, or explicit opt-in.
- Policy 2 (proxy-first): terminate in proxy by default for operational predictability; allow direct connect for customers with strict egress/IP requirements.
- Policy 3 (affinity + fallback): prefer direct when healthy; automatic failover to proxy when direct fails or exceeds latency bounds.

Priya: i'm leaning to Policy 3. gives best latency for normal ops and predictable fallback.

Matt: propose thresholds: direct preferred if sustained <200 rps and <5k tokens/minute. migrate to proxy when >200 rps sustained OR when customer requests caching/batching. numbers are negotiable.

Oliver: also add egress constraint: if downstream partner requires preserved source IP -> mandatory direct. mark this in onboarding QA checklist.

Devon: failure detection idea: measure p95 between our controlplane3eproxy3ecustomer. if proxy path latency > 120ms for 20s or proxy error rate >2% for 1m, fail open to direct when available.

Sarah: routing proto snippet:
```yaml
connectivity:
  default_mode: prefer_direct_with_proxy_fallback
  direct_to_proxy_threshold_rps: 200
  proxy_fail_latency_ms: 120
  proxy_fail_window_s: 20
  forced_direct_tags: ["egress-ip-preservation", "partner-required"]
```

Matt: note on cert modes: 1) mTLS end-to-end with proxy as TCP passthrough (best for DLP/e2e encryption), 2) TLS terminate at proxy + attestation token to control plane (best for observability). both valid; require opt-in policy.

Priya: operational checklist items:
- tagging: annotate traces with path=direct|proxy and record proxy instance id.
- capacity: autoscale groups for proxy need >30% headroom during business hours.
- onboarding: explicit question about downstream IP requirements and partner ACLs.

Devon: i'll run a microbenchmark that simulates 1000 tenants with mixture of load to validate autoscale knobs. will post numbers by Thu.

Sarah: decision actions: (1) adopt Policy 3 as default, (2) set threshold as Matt suggested as starting point, (3) onboarding form add egress-IP question, (4) Devon + Oliver run capacity/latency sims, (5) Priya to draft runbook for proxy failure and direct failover.

Matt: add: document cost model for both modes (annualized infra + ops). helps sales/solutions give customers a recommendation.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-3309: "Decision: tenant connectivity default (direct w/ proxy fallback) + follow-ups" assigned to Sarah, Devon, Oliver, Priya, Matt.

Oliver: small open question: do we allow customers to request proxied-only for GDPR/data-residency reasons? policy should allow explicit proxy-only flag.

Sarah: yes, add proxy-only opt in for data residency/compliance. will include in appendix.

Priya: i'll add monitoring dashboards: path split by customer, 95th latency per path, proxy error rates, and a failover alarm.

Devon: will post perf sim results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:
